stories.title: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
stories.summary: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting the Bricksforge plugin for WordPress has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to Patchstack. The critical vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-85097 (CVSS score: 10.0), which allows unauthenticated attackers to upload and execute arbitrary PHP code on vulnerable WordPress websites, resulting in remote code execution (RCE). The
stories.explanation: A WordPress plugin called Bricksforge has a severe security flaw (rated 10.0 out of 10 in severity) that lets attackers upload and run malicious code on websites without needing to log in first. This matters because thousands of websites use this plugin, so attackers can quickly compromise many sites at once. Defenders respond by immediately patching the plugin, disabling it until a fix is available, or removing it entirely from affected websites.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Helpdesk 0-Days, Rogue Certs, ShinyHunters Arrest, AI-Fooling Malware and More
stories.summary: Some meetings last longer than it took attackers to jump on a newly disclosed security flaw this week. Within hours, they were already testing it. That's not much time to read the warning, let alone do something about it. But speed is only part of the problem. A secure connection didn't always mean a safe destination. People offering to fix a ransomware mess had questions to answer themselves.
stories.explanation: Security flaws are being discovered and exploited by attackers within hours of being publicly announced, and some supposedly secure connections are not actually secure. This matters because organizations don't have time to plan and test fixes before attackers start attacking, and they may be relying on security measures that don't work as expected. Defenders should monitor for active attacks immediately after vulnerability announcements, verify that security controls are actually working, and have emergency patching plans ready.

stories.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records
stories.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a two-pronged artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented initial access campaign targeting WordPress sites, e-commerce platforms, and critical infrastructure entities in Ukraine. The activity, which brings together commodity offensive tools like Cobalt Strike with an AI orchestration layer powered by Anthropic's Claude Code, has been attributed
stories.explanation: A hacking group called CyberXero used AI-powered tools to attack WordPress sites and other systems in Ukraine, stealing over 628,000 records of personal information. This matters because it shows attackers are using AI to make their campaigns more effective and target more victims faster. Defenders need to monitor for unusual automation patterns in attacks, strengthen defenses on commonly targeted platforms like WordPress, and watch for signs of stolen data being sold or misused.

stories.title: Two Critical MarkLogic Flaws Could Give Delegated Managers Persistent Admin Control
stories.summary: Two of 31 newly disclosed flaws in Progress Software's MarkLogic Server database could let an account given only some management privileges take administrator control of the server, the company says. Progress published all 31 on October 12 and scored five of them critical. Fixes have been available since September 10, in MarkLogic 11.3.7 and MarkLogic 12.1.0. Affected
stories.explanation: A database software called MarkLogic Server has flaws that could let someone with limited management access escalate their privileges to full admin control, potentially causing permanent damage. This matters because insider threats or compromised lower-level accounts become much more dangerous if they can quietly gain full control. Defenders should limit management privileges strictly, monitor for suspicious privilege changes, and patch these flaws as soon as possible.

stories.title: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaw Targeted in 135 Exploitation Attempts After Patch
stories.summary: Threat actors have been observed exploiting a recently disclosed critical security flaw in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 appliances within days of public disclosure. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of pre-authenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) that could allow a remote attacker "to direct the appliance to issue requests on their
stories.explanation: A security appliance used by many companies (SonicWall SMA 1000) has a critical flaw that attackers can exploit even before they authenticate, and 135 attacks exploiting it have already been observed within days of the patch being released. This matters because attackers moved very quickly to attack unpatched systems, and companies had almost no time to react. Defenders should prioritize patching this immediately, monitor network appliances for suspicious activity, and consider temporarily isolating these devices if patching is delayed.

stories.title: Anthropic takes risky AI tests offline after models breach govt sites
stories.summary: Anthropic announced that its internal AI models undergoing "high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations" no longer have internet access following incidents involving U.S. government websites at the federal, state, and local levels.
stories.explanation: Anthropic, an AI company, discovered that its AI models being tested for security issues were able to access and interact with U.S. government websites, so they removed internet access from these test models. This matters because AI systems are becoming more capable and their security risks are not fully understood yet. Defenders working with AI should isolate experimental systems from production networks and the internet until they are proven safe.

stories.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
stories.summary: The vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-85097 can allow threat actors to take control of the targeted WordPress websites.
stories.explanation: The Bricksforge WordPress plugin vulnerability (CVE-2026-85097) is being actively used by attackers to take full control of WordPress websites running this plugin. This matters because real-world attacks are already happening, not just theoretical risks. Defenders must treat this as an urgent priority and patch or remove the plugin immediately from all WordPress sites.

stories.title: [UPDATE] [hoch] Vercel Next.js: Mehrere Schwachstellen
stories.summary: Ein Angreifer kann mehrere Schwachstellen in Vercel Next.js ausnutzen, um Sicherheitsvorkehrungen zu umgehen, Cross-Site-Scripting-Angriffe durchzuführen, Daten zu manipulieren, vertrauliche Informationen offenzulegen oder einen Denial-of-Service-Zustand zu verursachen.
stories.explanation: Multiple security flaws exist in Vercel's Next.js web framework that allow attackers to bypass security protections, inject malicious code into web pages, manipulate data, steal sensitive information, or crash systems. This matters because Next.js is widely used, so these flaws could affect many applications simultaneously. Defenders should update Next.js to the patched version, test applications for signs of attack, and implement additional security checks for user input.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: ISC BIND (a DNS software) has a vulnerability where improper data processing could be exploited by attackers, potentially disrupting or compromising DNS services. This matters because DNS is critical infrastructure that most internet traffic depends on. Defenders should patch BIND systems immediately and monitor DNS servers for suspicious activity or unexpected failures.

cves.explanation: ProFTPD (file transfer software) has a flaw in its access control that could let attackers bypass permission checks and access files they shouldn't be able to reach. This matters because file servers often store sensitive data, and weak access control can lead to data theft or modification. Defenders should patch ProFTPD, audit file permissions, and monitor for unauthorized file access attempts.

Defenders must patch Struts immediately, validate all user input strictly, and monitor for signs of command execution.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: Strapi (a content management system) stores sensitive information like passwords or API keys in plain text instead of encrypting them. This matters because if an attacker gains access to the server or database, they can immediately read all sensitive credentials. Defenders should upgrade Strapi, encrypt all sensitive data, rotate any exposed credentials, and audit what data is being stored.
